findings.rationale: class 1 (define-before-use; Abstract, main.tex:L28): 'card' is used for a share from the abstract onward and is never defined anywhere (Section 4.1 starts with 'a number of cards' as if known).
findings.suggested_fix: Say once, at first use, that a card is one share: one written phrase of the set.

findings.rationale: class 1 (define-before-use; Abstract, main.tex:L29): 'spare card' is never defined; the reader has to infer that it means a card beyond the threshold t that is present at recovery.
findings.suggested_fix: Define it at first use: 'spare cards (those beyond the t needed)'.

findings.evidence_span: the grid decoder with its digest
findings.rationale: class 1 (define-before-use; Abstract, main.tex:L35): 'digest' appears in the abstract with no gloss and is only defined in Section 4.3; the introduction calls the same thing 'a hash check on the shared secret'.
findings.suggested_fix: Write 'with a shared hash of the secret (the digest)' in the abstract and use 'digest' in the introduction.

findings.rationale: class 1 (define-before-use; Abstract, main.tex:L26): 'edit' is used in the abstract but 'edit hypotheses' and what counts as an edit are defined only in Section 3.2.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with 'by a small search over such edits' so the word is anchored to the list just given.

findings.evidence_span: A secret that no vendor can reset
findings.rationale: class 1 (define-before-use; Abstract, main.tex:L19): 'secret' is used in an ordinary sense for four pages before Section 4.1 (line 211) gives it a technical definition (the 24 mnemonic words, not the BIP39 seed).
findings.suggested_fix: Move the 'secret = the mnemonic words, not the seed' sentence to the introduction.

findings.rationale: class 1 (define-before-use; Abstract, main.tex:L31): The abstract's four percentages name their comparison and the m-of-n set but not the card design (k=4 parity words, 30-word cards) they were measured on.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'with 30-word cards (k=4)' to the sentence.

findings.rationale: class 1 (define-before-use; Abstract, main.tex:L35): The 31,600 total has no referent the reader can check: it is quoted in the abstract, Section 5.3 and the conclusion, but what it counts (every row of six output files, including rows no table prints) is only said in Section 8, line 724.
findings.suggested_fix: State at line 566 what the total sums over, or quote a total that the printed tables add up to.

findings.rationale: class 1 (define-before-use; 1 Introduction, main.tex:L48): 'product code' is used in the introduction's central claim and again in the proof of Proposition 1(d) without ever being defined; the declared audience is only assumed to know basic Reed-Solomon.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one clause: 'a product code (an array whose every row is a codeword of one code and every column a codeword of another)'.

findings.rationale: class 1 (define-before-use; 1 Introduction, main.tex:L56): 41 of 92 is 45%, which matches neither the 40% (three days) nor the 49% (seven days) just quoted, so the reader cannot tell which failure the 41 refers to.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the test the 41 failed, or give the counts behind the 40% and 49%.

findings.rationale: class 1 (define-before-use; 1 Introduction, main.tex:L85): 'header' is used as a known term, but the bullet above only spoke of 'one unprinted symbol that carries its number'; the name is introduced in Section 4.1 (line 218).
findings.suggested_fix: Name it in the bullet: 'one unprinted symbol, the header, that carries its number'.

findings.rationale: class 1 (define-before-use; 3.2 Repair beyond substitutions, main.tex:L200): The 'N+k' shorthand (24+2, and the 12+2 ... 24+4 column heads of Table 1) is never introduced.
findings.suggested_fix: Write 'a phrase of 24 data and 2 parity words (written 24+2)' at first use.

findings.evidence_span: unconfirmed evidence under the number entered
findings.rationale: class 1 (define-before-use; 4.2 Reading the header, main.tex:L301): 'unconfirmed evidence' (and 'confirmed') are decoder states defined only in Section 4.4 step 1 (line 333), after this use.
findings.suggested_fix: Move this sentence into Section 4.4 or add a forward pointer with a three-word gloss.

findings.rationale: class 1 (define-before-use; 5.2 Single phrases (Table 1), main.tex:L461): The '2 dropped words' cells at k=2 (0 / 1 and 0 / 30) are neither 100 nor 'refused', and the text, which lists the beyond-capacity rows, never says what the remaining trials returned.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence saying whether those trials were ambiguous, wrong or refused.

findings.evidence_span: \emph{Card parity}: each card is repaired alone
findings.rationale: class 2 (naming drift; 5.1 Setup, main.tex:L409): One baseline has many names: 'repairing cards separately' (abstract), 'Card parity' (tables, legend), 'per-card repair' (Figure 2 caption, 5.3), 'repairing cards one at a time', 'repair card by card', 'per-share correction'; the Figure 2 caption and its legend disagree.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick 'per-card repair' or 'Card parity' and use it in the text, caption and legend.

findings.rationale: class 2 (naming drift; 3.1 The code, main.tex:L143): The single-phrase object is called 'protected phrase', 'parity phrases' (line 73, undefined), 'single phrases', 'an unshared 24-word phrase' and 'single-phrase format', alongside 'mnemonic'.
findings.suggested_fix: Define one name ('parity phrase') here and use it throughout.

findings.evidence_span: the number of edits plus substitutions
findings.rationale: class 2 (naming drift; 3.2 Repair beyond substitutions, main.tex:L187): 'edit' excludes substitutions here, but 'the two-edit rows' (line 437, which include '1 wrong + 1 dropped') and 'every single edit' (line 693) count a wrong word as an edit.
findings.suggested_fix: Say 'edits (swaps, drops, insertions)' versus 'substitutions' consistently, or call them all edits.

findings.rationale: class 2 (naming drift; 4.4 Decoding, main.tex:L331): 'row' means the unwritten coefficient rows r_0..r_{t-1} in Section 4.1, a card in the decoder steps and in 'no spare rows' (line 576), and a table row in Section 5 ('the 3-of-5 row').
findings.suggested_fix: Reserve 'row' for r_d, say 'card' in the decoder steps, and 'table row' in Section 5.

findings.rationale: class 2 (naming drift; 5.4 With exactly t cards, main.tex:L576): 'spare rows' is a one-off variant of 'spare cards'.
findings.suggested_fix: Write 'no spare cards'.

findings.rationale: class 2 (naming drift; 5.1 Setup, main.tex:L384): 'wrong' is an outcome label with two different definitions (grids: a different secret returned; single phrases: only other phrases offered) and is also the ordinary adjective in 'wrong word', 'wrong number' and 'Wrong cards' (line 545, meaning foreign or garbage).
findings.suggested_fix: Give the outcomes distinct names (e.g. 'miscorrected') and keep 'wrong' for words.

findings.evidence_span: nothing if one card is lost or burnt
findings.rationale: class 2 (naming drift; 6 Custody Arrangements, main.tex:L643): 'burnt' here reads as a destroyed card, but 'burn' was defined (line 395) as a run of unreadable words on a card and the table's 'Burnt' column is five such words on every card; 'burn', 'burnt', 'unreadable', 'missing' and 'illegible' also alternate.
findings.suggested_fix: Write 'if one card is lost, or if every card has a five-word burn' and keep 'burn' for runs only.

findings.evidence_span: \emph{Checksum only}: a card counts only if
findings.rationale: class 2 (naming drift; 5.1 Setup, main.tex:L406): 'Checksum only' names a method that uses the card's parity words as a detector; 'checksum' elsewhere means the BIP39 SHA-256 checksum, SLIP39's RS1024 and codex32's BCH, and the method is later called 'a detection checksum'.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the column 'Detect only' or state in the definition that the card's own parity plays the checksum's role.

findings.evidence_span: A \emph{dealing} is one run of the following procedure
findings.rationale: class 2 (naming drift; 4.1 Construction, main.tex:L214): After 'dealing' is defined, the same group of cards is still called a 'set' (3-of-5 set), a 'sharing', a 'Scheme' (Table 4 column) and an 'arrangement', while 'arrangement' also means the grid layout (line 236) and a custody plan (Section 6).
findings.suggested_fix: Use 'dealing' for one issued group, 't-of-n set' for the parameters, and keep 'arrangement' for Section 6.

findings.rationale: class 2 (naming drift; 4.1 Construction, main.tex:L261): People are 'holders', 'party', 'participant', 'person/people', 'owner'; and m counts shares (line 116), holders (here) and confirmed cards (line 355).
findings.suggested_fix: Use 'holder' for a person and let m count cards present at recovery throughout.

findings.rationale: class 2 (naming drift; 5.2 Single phrases, main.tex:L431): Condition (2) is 'the standard guarantee' in Section 3.1, 'the capacity' here and 'within capacity' in Section 7, and is distinct from 'this bound' of Proposition 1(d).
findings.suggested_fix: Name (2) 'the capacity' where it is displayed.

findings.rationale: class 2 (naming drift; 4.4 Decoding, main.tex:L332): The filter of line 190 is 'the BIP39 filter', 'the BIP39 checksum as a filter' and 'the filter' in turn.
findings.suggested_fix: Name it once at line 190 ('the BIP39 filter') and reuse.

findings.evidence_span: Across all 31{,}600 grid trials in this paper
findings.rationale: class 5 (results before objects; 5.3 Grids, main.tex:L566): The pooled no-wrong-answer result is drawn over Table 3 and Table 4 runs (and unprinted rows) that the reader has not yet met.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the pooled statement after Section 6, or restrict this sentence to the Table 2 trials.

findings.rationale: class 5 (results before objects; 4.2 Reading the header, main.tex:L301): A statement about the experiments appears in the construction section, three pages before the experiments and their fault list exist.
findings.suggested_fix: Move it next to 'Card numbers are otherwise given correctly' in Section 5.1.

findings.rationale: class 6 (repeated caveats; Table 3 caption, main.tex:L585): The no-wrong-secret result is stated in the abstract, in 5.3 (line 566), in the captions of Tables 3 and 4, and in the conclusion.
findings.suggested_fix: State it once in 5.3 with its bound and drop it from the captions.

findings.evidence_span: $t$ cards there are no spare rows, the grid decoder equals per-card repair
findings.rationale: class 6 (repeated caveats; 5.4 With exactly t cards, main.tex:L576): 'With exactly t cards joint decoding adds nothing' is restated in full in the abstract, the introduction (line 80), 5.3 (line 553), here, Section 6 (lines 642, 657), Section 7 (line 692) and the conclusion.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the abstract, this subsection and one planning rule; cut the rest to cross-references.

findings.evidence_span: (1) Word error rates of 1--10\% are an assumption.
findings.rationale: class 6 (repeated caveats; 7 Discussion, main.tex:L677): The caveat that copying error rates are unmeasured is given in the introduction twice (lines 53 and 87), here, and again under Open directions (line 699).
findings.suggested_fix: Keep lines 53 and 677; delete the other two.

findings.evidence_span: We give no formal proofs of the implementation
findings.rationale: class 6 (repeated caveats; 1 Introduction, main.tex:L86): The not-verified caveat recurs at line 680 ('tested, not verified ... no theorem about the decoder is proved') and line 700.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep it in Section 7 only.

findings.evidence_span: (4) The grid decoder is a heuristic.
findings.rationale: class 6 (repeated caveats; 7 Discussion, main.tex:L683): Repeats the caveat of lines 286-287 that the decoder is not shown to reach the Proposition 1(d) bound, and restates the set-aside rule of 4.4 and 5.3.
findings.suggested_fix: Point back to Section 4.1 instead of restating.

findings.evidence_span: returned no wrong secret in 31{,}600 trials
findings.rationale: class 6 (repeated caveats; 9 Conclusion, main.tex:L739): The conclusion's closing sentences repeat the abstract's last two sentences nearly verbatim.
findings.suggested_fix: End the conclusion on the planning consequence instead of the trial count.

findings.rationale: class 6 (repeated caveats; 4.1 Construction, main.tex:L212): An unprompted denial in parentheses interrupts the first sentence of the construction.
findings.suggested_fix: Fold it into the definition: 'the secret, i.e. the mnemonic words themselves'.

findings.evidence_span: repairing cards one at a time recovers 31\%
findings.rationale: class 7 (number variants; 5.3 Grids, main.tex:L526): Text and abstract round to integers (31%, 41%, 61%) while Table 2 prints truncated one-decimal values (30.5, 40.7, 61.2), and the Figure 2 caption says 'gains 20 points' for 61.2 minus 40.7; no sentence bridges the two conventions.
findings.suggested_fix: Quote the table values, or say once that the text rounds table entries to the nearest integer.

findings.rationale: class 7 (number variants; 5.3 Grids, main.tex:L539): Within one paragraph some table entries are rounded (86, 93; also 90 and 98 at line 533) and others are quoted to one decimal (92.5, 94.7, 98.2).
findings.suggested_fix: Use one precision in running text.

findings.rationale: class 7 (number variants; 6 Custody Arrangements, main.tex:L643): The same configuration (3-of-5, exactly three cards, 3% wrong) is 85% in Section 5.4, 84.5 in Tables 2 and 3 and 83% (83.2) here, and the next sentence quotes 98.8% unrounded; the bridge about repeated runs is back at line 423.
findings.suggested_fix: Add '(Table 4; a separate run from Table 2)' here.

findings.rationale: class 7 (number variants; 5.3 Grids, main.tex:L547): The range is the bracketed 67 / 59.7 of Table 2 rounded and reordered, so the reader has to hunt for the cells.

findings.evidence_span: $k=6$ or more when recovery from exactly $t$ cards
findings.rationale: class 7 (number variants; 7 Discussion, main.tex:L692): The advice for the exactly-t case is 'k=8 restores 99%' (line 579), 'k=6 or k=8' (line 647) and 'k=6 or more' here.
findings.suggested_fix: Give one recommendation and cite Table 3 for it.

findings.rationale: class 4 (float proximity; 5.2 Single phrases, main.tex:L443): Table 1 is discussed in Section 5.2 on page 7 but prints on page 8 together with Table 2, after Section 5.3 has begun.
findings.suggested_fix: Place Table 1 before the 5.3 heading (e.g. top of page 7 or a float barrier).

findings.rationale: class 4 (float proximity; 5.3 Grids, main.tex:L513): Figure 2 is cited and its 99.5/31 and 61/41 points are discussed on page 7, but it prints on page 9, two pages on, directly above Section 5.4.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the figure ahead of Table 2 or onto the page of the 'Spare cards' paragraph.

findings.rationale: class 9 (narrative placement; 2 Related Work, main.tex:L90): Related work sits between the introduction and the construction and already compares against undefined objects ('the property our cards have at the word level', line 109; 'our first parity check is the plain sum', line 128).
findings.suggested_fix: Move the section after Section 4, or strip the comparisons that need the construction.

findings.rationale: class 9 (narrative placement; 4.5 Why not split one long phrase?, main.tex:L360): A motivation for the whole grid design arrives after the construction, proposition and decoder, as the last thing before the experiments.
findings.suggested_fix: Move it to the start of Section 4 or into the Discussion.

findings.rationale: class 9 (narrative placement; 4.1 Construction, main.tex:L219): The header is introduced with no sentence saying what it is for; its purpose (binding card number and threshold into the codeword) has to be pieced together from the remark after Proposition 1 and Section 4.2.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one 'why' sentence here.

findings.rationale: class 9 (narrative placement; 8 Reproducibility, main.tex:L702): A page of build commands and file names sits between the Discussion and the Conclusion, and it carries the only definition of the 31,600 total.
findings.suggested_fix: Move it after the Conclusion as an appendix and keep the trial-count definition in Section 5.

findings.evidence_span: most 14 columns are unsettled, guess a set of 3 to $k$
findings.rationale: class 9 (narrative placement; 4.4 Decoding, main.tex:L344): The rescue step packs four unexplained thresholds (one short of t, k>=3, 14 columns, 3 to k) into one sentence with no reason for any of them.
findings.suggested_fix: Split the step and give a clause of rationale for the limits, or call them implementation limits.

findings.evidence_span: The tighter limit on swaps is necessary.
findings.rationale: class 9 (narrative placement; 3.2 Repair beyond substitutions, main.tex:L194): One paragraph carries a full counting argument (syndrome ratio, locator, 325 swaps, expected 4) in running prose, and it is the only place the reader learns why the swap rule differs.
findings.suggested_fix: Lead with the conclusion ('otherwise about four swaps per phrase would miscorrect') and set the arithmetic off after it.
